In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of new organosilicon and organoboron compounds with interesting structures, properties and reactivities.
the synthesis and characterization of new organometallic compounds with unusual bonding and reactivity patterns.
the synthesis and reactivity of novel silicon-containing molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dicationic charge of the tetrasilacyclobutadiene is delocalized over the Si(4), and the amidinate moieties are involved in the charge stabilization of the cationic core, as indicated by the NMR and DFT results.
a Lewis acid assisted silylene dimerization reaction has led to the formation of a donor-stobilized tetrasilabicyclo[1.1.0]butane-1,4-dication.
a donor-stabilization of a tetrasilacyclotetraenium cation is not possible, but the formation of a donor-stablized tetrasilabutadienium dication is feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a Lewis acid assisted silylene reaction with Cp*ZnCl(3) is a new synthetic route to donor-stabilized silylium species, which can be used as a new type of silylene source.
we have successfully developed the first Lewis acid assisted reaction for N-heterocycle silylene.

the N-donor stabilized tetrasilacyclobutadiene dication represents a new member of the family of donor-stabilized silylium species and that the N-donors are not only capable of stabilizing the silylium cations but also of stabilizing the tetrasilacyclodiene dications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-heteroaromatic ligand of a chloro silyene plays an important role in stabilizing the Si(4)-based dicationic species, which is otherwise difficult to obtain.
the Lewis acidity of the Cp*Zr(III) center is sufficient to activate a chloro silyene to undergo an unusual 1,2-Cl migration, leading to the formation of a stable donor-stabilized Si(4) cation.
the formation of a tetrasilacylobutadiene species is possible by a reaction between a chloro silyene and a Lewis acidic metal center.
